title: After the fall: a prior grace that determines the will
source_text: III. Ex quo vero homo in peccatum lapsus est, juxta doctorum istorum sententiam, fieri non potest ut ad Deum se convertat, aut jam conversus ad bonum aliquod opus se moveat, sine praevio quodam gratiae auxilio, quo non simpliciter ad bonum invitetur & sollicitetur, aut etiam in bono opere adjuvetur, sed quo voluntas ejus ad bonum flectatur atque determinetur, & bonus volendi actus efficaciter in ea producatur. Id enim exigere voluntatis infirmitatem, quam prava concupiscentia in homine post peccatum inhaerens, continuo pondere ad terrena incurvat, & quae propterea ad singulos dilectionis coelestis impetus, actuali & efficaci Dei auxilio sursum erigi opus habet.
pass_a_gloss: III. But from the time that man has fallen into sin, according to the opinion of these doctors, it cannot be that he turn himself to God, or already converted move himself to some good work, without a certain prior help of grace, by which he is not simply invited and solicited to good, or also helped in the good work, but by which his will is bent and determined to good, and the good act of willing is efficaciously produced in it. For this, they say, the infirmity of the will requires, which depraved concupiscence inhering in man after sin bends down with continual weight to earthly things, and which therefore for each impulse of heavenly love has need to be raised upward by the actual and efficacious help of God.
pass_b_english: Thesis III. Once a person has fallen into sin, these doctors hold, he cannot turn to God, nor, once converted, set himself to any good work, without some prior aid of grace. This aid does not merely invite and urge him toward the good, or assist him while he does a good work; it bends and determines his will toward the good and effectively produces in it a good act of willing.

They say the weakness of the will demands this. Corrupt concupiscence, clinging to a person after sin, keeps dragging the will down toward earthly things by its constant weight, so that for every single impulse of heavenly love it must be lifted upward by God's actual and efficacious help.
